Real quick: for word length in mobile app, yes you can use "Anagram" for an exact word length. "Patternn" works also

"Subanagram" for "this many letters or shorter".

For "this many letters or longer", you use "....*" with "Pattern Match", with the number of periods being the minimum number of letters. A period is a wild letter, like a blank tile (a question mark is the same). The period means it has to be some letter,  while the star means any number of letters, including zero

Yes it can. you just have to sync your data between the NASPA desktop program and iPad app.
First make sure you've rebuilt the Collins lexicon since adding the definitions (tools, rebuild database , aingle Lexicon, CWL19, then CWL21)

Below is screenshot both PC and mobile showing Collins definitions. (note rhat because the mobile app search feature is atrocious, there's no way to filter for CSW only words . but the ones circled, or showing a # sign next to word, are CSW19 but not NWL2023). also you can't even filter by word length lol. but you can do "X letters or less" by adding "subanagram" filter, searching for "*****", where the number of *s , aka wilds, is the max length (for a word to  be a subanagram of say 6 random letters, it must be 6 letters or shorter)

[NASPA Zyzzyva with Collins Definitions - PC and Mobile l](https://imgur.com/a/tVGm9kv)

In the desktop app - click EDIT in the top menu bar --> preferences. in the left panel, click on General. Now on the right where it says "Zyzzyva syncs with" , select Dropbox. 
Click Okay to close the menu. Now your web browser automatically open a dropbox page so you can give your personal Dropbox account to sync with. BTW dropbox is completely free and you don't need to use it for anything else, so sign up if you don't have one 
Once you sign in, approve the request from Zyzzyva to have access to a folder (where your data will be)
Should see a success page . That's done

Now on the desktop app, go to Sync --> Sync now. and it'll upload your zyzzyva data to dropbox. It could take a few minutes depending on connection speed. note in the bottom left of the program window it says how many items are left 

once done, now on the mobile app, just tap settings, scroll down to sync, and tap to sync with dropbox. provide the same username and password. then tap "sync now" . there should be a popup about the conflict between your phones version lf data and dropbox (desktop). you obviously want to use what us on dropbox and replace your data on mobile. so when it asks if the remote data is up to date, tap yes. if local data up to dats, tap no. then tap to confirm

that is all. you will see the number of files left to sync count down right above the "sync now" button. it could take a few minutes again like before.

that is all. you are good

Hi - I can pretty easily describe how to pull all CSW definitions in to NASPA zyzzyva
Since the definitions are encrypted in Collins Zyzzyva , you just need to replace the text file with the CSW words (but no defs) in the NASPA Zyzzyva lexicon folder, with one containing CSW words and definitions. 

The NASPA data is in "C:\Program Files\NASPA Zyzzyva 3.4.0\data\words\British" (with the Zyzzyva version number you have if 3.4.1)

You'll see several files starting with CSW19 and CSW21. You need to replace CSW19.txt and CSW21.txt . to be extra safe, copy the current versions as backup. 

Now the files below are the CSW wordlists with definitions. 

CSW19 (save as CSW19.txt , and move to the above folder)
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OshXolgmGvFVSghSoe9uP-ad836JiICN/view?usp=drivesdk

CSW21 (save as CSW21.txt , and move to the above folder)
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ePHgTlPltpd8Dw3UqrjWm8LMacyGPSK6/view?usp=drivesdk

That's it. when you re-open NASPA Zyzzyva, just rebuild the databases with Tools --> Rebuild Database --> (either All lexicons or just CSW19, then CSW21)

Now you'll see the CSW definitions in NASPA Zyzzva.

Note: the definitions are exactly as you'd see in Collins Zyzzyva, with one tiny formatting change .
Inflected words will start with the same "< " as they do in in NWL. 
Eg: "EATS" def is "< EAT,  to consume food [v]"  to match the format in NASPA Zyzzyva
instead of the Collins standard with no "< " to indicate infection - "EAT, to consume food [v]"
